plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the agent–environment interaction loop in reinforcement learning, depicted as a closed directed cycle between two rounded rectangular boxes filled with light teal. The upper box is labeled “Agent” with the policy π[a_t | s_t] inscribed inside, and the lower, larger box is labeled “Environment” with the state transition probability Pr(s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t) inscribed inside. Orange arrows with arrowheads form the loop: one arrow routes from the Agent box rightward and downward into the Environment box, carrying the action a_t; a second arrow returns from the Environment to the Agent carrying the current state s_t, while a third routes the next state s_{t+1} back around; additional arrow paths carry rewards r_t and r_{t+1}, and a label identifies the reward function Pr(r_{t+1} | s_t, a_t). Small white-background rectangles along the arrow paths isolate variable labels — State, Action, and Reward — for readability. This figure introduces the Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework at the core of reinforcement learning, showing how the agent observes a state, selects an action according to its policy, and receives a reward and next state from the environment in a repeating closed loop.

interactionPlan.concept: A reinforcement-learning agent and environment form a repeating Markov Decision Process loop: the agent observes a state, chooses an action from its policy, and the environment returns a reward and next state.

interactions.label: Animate one MDP time step
interactions.teaches: The learner understands the temporal order of one reinforcement-learning update: state reaches the agent, the policy selects an action, and the environment produces the next state and reward before the loop repeats
Clicking the Agent emphasizes that the policy π[a_t | s_t] is the decision rule that maps the observed state to an action sent to the environment
Clicking the Environment emphasizes that both the next-state distribution and the reward distribution depend on the current state-action pair

demo_steps.title: Observe the current state
demo_steps.narration: The loop begins when the agent receives the current state s_t, along with the reward signal r_t from the previous transition. These are the agent's inputs before it chooses what to do next.

demo_steps.title: Choose an action
demo_steps.narration: Click the Agent to focus on the policy π[a_t | s_t]. The policy uses the current state to select or sample the action a_t that flows back toward the environment.

demo_steps.title: Update through the environment
demo_steps.narration: Click the Environment to highlight the state transition and reward functions. Given s_t and a_t, the environment generates s_{t+1} and r_{t+1}.

demo_steps.title: Close the loop
demo_steps.narration: Play the animation to see the complete cycle: s_t enters the agent, a_t returns to the environment, and the resulting s_{t+1} and r_{t+1} become the next inputs.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: In an MDP, the agent controls actions through its policy, while the environment controls the next state and reward conditioned on the current state and action.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate a clean 2D flow diagram on a white background. Place the Agent box near the top center and the larger Environment box below it, both filled light teal with black outlines and rounded corners. Use muted orange orthogonal arrow paths with arrowheads to form a closed loop around and between the boxes. Keep the math labels legible in black, with small white rectangular masks behind labels that sit on top of arrows. During the animation, use a bright highlight or moving pulse along the relevant arrow segment in sequence: state/reward into Agent, action out of Agent, state/action into Environment, then next state and reward returning for the following time step. Clicking Agent should brighten the Agent box, policy label, and action arrow; clicking Environment should brighten the Environment box, transition probability label, reward probability label, and the returned next-state/reward arrows.
